verdict.rationale: The SDK supports pausing a run and resuming from a serialized `RunState` when a tool call needs approval (human-in-the-loop), which could in principle survive a restart, but this is a narrow interruption mechanism rather than general crash-safe checkpointing of arbitrary run state. Community discussion notes that full durable execution (e.g., surviving crashes) is achieved by wrapping the SDK in an external durability engine like Temporal, implying native checkpoint/resume-on-crash is not a first-class built-in feature.
